title: Genevieve Nnaji
markdown:
In 2009, Nnaji was one of the highest-paid female actors in Nollywood.\[24\]\[25\] Due to her contributions to the Nigerian movie industry, she became the first actor to be awarded Best Actress at the 2001 *City People*'s Awards, the award ceremony that previously had only recognised politicians and business conglomerates. She was also the first actor to be awarded Best Actress by the Censors Board of Nigeria in 2003.\[26\] In 2009, she was referred to as the Julia Roberts of Africa by Oprah Winfrey.\[27\]\[28\]

In November 2015, Nnaji produced her first movie called *Road to Yesterday*,\[29\] later winning Best Movie Overall - West Africa at the 2016 Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards.\[30\]

In January 2018, it was reported that Nnaji would be replacing Funke Akindele as a member of the Dora Milaje in Marvel's *Avengers: Infinity War*. This was later debunked as an internet prank, and the actor did not appear in the movie.\[31\]

On 7 September 2018, her directorial debut *Lionheart* was acquired by online streaming service Netflix, making it the first Netflix original film from Nigeria.\[32\] The movie premiered at the 2018 Toronto International Film Festival, where she also appeared in Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje's autobiographical directorial debut *Farming*, alongside Kate Beckinsale, Damson Idris, and Gugu Mbatha-Raw.\[33\]

In 2023, it was announced that Nnaji would return as an executive film producer with *I Do Not Come to You by Chance*, an adaptation of the novel by Adaobi Tricia Nwaubani, alongside Chinny Carter. The film features Blossom Chukwujekwu, Paul Nnadiekwe, Jennifer Eliogu, Sambasa Nzeribe, and Beverly Osu. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival but has not yet been officially released.\[34\]\[35\]\[36\]

Nnaji is also a women's activist. She advocates for Nigerian girls to be able to have a say in who they choose to marry. She is against early marriages for the girl child. She advocates against the abuse of women in society.\[37\]\[38\]\[39\] Nnaji has described herself as a feminist, stating that her type of feminism is that of a woman who has the right to make her own choices and do whatever she feels like.\[40\]

In May 2026, Nnaji was named among the six honorees for the Women in Cinema Gala hosted by the Red Sea Film Foundation during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival.\[41\]

### Modelling

Nnaji in one of her several modelling campaigns.

Nnaji has featured in several commercials, including Pronto (beverage) and Omo detergent. In 2004, she became the "Face of Lux" in Nigeria.\[42\]\[9\] In 2008, Nnaji launched the clothing line "St. Genevieve", which donates its proceeds to charity.\[8\]\[43\] In May 2010, she was appointed as the "Face of MUD" in Nigeria.\[44\]\[45\]\[46\]\[47\]\[48\]
